exposure: in vitro fertilization/intracytoplasmic sperm injection-embryo transfer (IVF/ICSI-ET)
cohort: 834 women who underwent IVF or ICSI treatment between 2015 and 2019 with a delivery history
finding: The presence of a caesarean section defect (CSD) in women, especially those aged ≤ 35 years, was associated with significantly lower live birth rates and mean implantation rates after IVF/ICSI compared to women with a previous vaginal delivery, while a history of CS without a defect did not affect IVF/ICSI outcomes.
mod_finding: This study found that the existence of a Cesarean scar without a defect does not decrease the live birth rate after IVF or ICSI compared with a previous vaginal delivery, while the presence of a Cesarean section defect, especially in younger women, significantly impaired chances of subsequent pregnancy.
